title: GPO Studio remediation scenario v1
description: A durable, provenance-annotated scenario describing expected Windows behavior for a capability that diverged (or may diverge) from Windows reality. Scenarios are data: they name what an operator means, what native Windows tooling does with it, and which test platform proves the two agree. The JSON schema is the cheap structural gate; gpo_studio.remediation_corpus performs the real validation (referential integrity, per-family payload shape, anchor hashes).

scenario_id.description: Unique identifier; stable forever once oracle evidence cites it

family.description: Remediation family. Adding a family requires a schema enum entry, a loader validator branch, and a remediation-corpus.md section.

readiness.description: ready = executable against a qualified platform today; blocked = a platform or evidence gap is recorded in blocked_reason

blocked_reason.description: Required when readiness is blocked; must name the gap, not the hope

work_items.description: Tracked work items this scenario supplies evidence for

tier.description: native-observation = anchored to captured native tooling output; spec-informed = derived from MS-* documentation, not yet captured; hypothesis = believed, must be proven before any claim

note.description: How this knowledge was obtained and why the tier is honest

path.description: Repository-relative path to the anchor artifact

sha256.description: Required for native-capture anchors; verified by the loader so a changed capture breaks the corpus loudly

lane.description: Lane id from platforms.json; binds hosts, tools, and oracle

boundaries.description: Subset of the lane's boundaries from boundary-matrix.md; one scenario may assert several boundaries but each is reported separately

authored_intent.description: Family-shaped: what an operator means. Per-family required keys are enforced by gpo_studio.remediation_corpus.

expected_native.description: Family-shaped: the machine-checkable native Windows behavior the oracle must observe. Per-family required keys are enforced by gpo_studio.remediation_corpus.

open_questions.description: Explicit unknowns. An open question is a healthy corpus state; an unrecorded wrong assumption is not.

predictions_before_the_run.description: What was believed BEFORE the estate was touched, for a scenario that asks an open question rather than confirming an expectation. Optional, and only meaningful on a `hypothesis`-tier scenario. It exists because a prediction written after the fact is not a prediction: WI-040's arc (predict, observe, let the divergence be the finding) is the discipline this project keeps having to re-learn, and prose in a commit message is not somewhere a later reader will look. The two halves are separate because they are DIFFERENT CLAIMS -- what Studio's model says, and what the physics argues -- and collapsing them hides the case where the model is right for the wrong reason.

recorded.description: When this was written down, and the assertion that it predates estate contact

verdict_expected.description: The lane verdict expected from the first execution. An `inconclusive` here is a legitimate and expected outcome for an open-question scenario, not a defect to be designed away.

model.description: What Studio's model answers today. May be an abstention, which is an admission rather than a prediction about Windows.

physics.description: What the documented mechanism argues Windows will do. An argument, not a measurement -- which is exactly why it is recorded before the run.
